To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the dq0 reference frame is a valid representation for split-phase machines; (b) the dq equivalent circuit representation is valid only if N is equal to or less than 2; and (c) the dq equivalent representation is valid also for N>2 if cross couplings between the d and q axes are included in the equivalent circuit.

(i) the dq0 reference frame representation can be applied to an arbitrary number N of three-phase sets; (ii) the equivalent circuit representation is not unique and depends on the number of three-phase sets.

the dq equivalent circuit representation of a split-phase machine is not decoupled when N is higher than or equal 3, and that the cross coupling terms are a function of the number of stator phases, of the stator winding distribution and of the number of independent inverters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a complete dq equivalent circuit representation for an arbitrary number of three-phase sets in a split-phase machine.
a systematic approach to the modeling and control of split-phase machines with arbitrary number N of stator sets.
the development of a general equivalent circuit model of split-phase machines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, as long as N=2, dq equivalent circuit representations are still useful for split-phase machines.
the equivalent circuit representation of a split-phase machine can be reduced to a single dq equivalent circuit for N=1 and to N single dq circuits for N=2.
the equivalent circuit representation is not a good choice for split-phase machines with N higher than or equals to 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, as long as a dq reference frame is used to model a split-phase machine in the N=1 or N=2 case, it can be represented by a decoupled equivalent circuit.

a split-phase machine can be represented by a dq equivalent circuit in the same way as a three-phase machine, but with an additional number of branches equal to N - 1, where N is the number of stator three-phase sets.
the proposed equivalent circuits are valid for any N, and the number of branches is the minimum one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed equivalent circuit representation can be applied to any number of three-phase sets.
the proposed equivalent circuits, which are based on the dq0 reference frame representation, can be applied to any number of stator three-phase sets.

, in order to correctly model a multi-set split-phase machine, the dq equivalent circuit representation must be extended to include the cross coupling terms between dq axes, which are neglected when the number of stator three-phase sets is equal to 2.
